newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli official cites information on more attacks.
newsitem.headline: Israeli official cites information on more attacks.

text.p: A top security official said on Sunday Israel had information pointing to the possibility of more suicide attacks by Islamic militants after last week's Jerusalem market bombing.

Asked if Israel had specific information about more attacks, police chief Assaf Hefetz told army radio: "It's more than just an estimate. We have a series of...details that point to this possibility."
Authorities have deployed more police in main cities and along the boundary between Israel and the West Bank to prevent militants from entering the Jewish state.
The army said troops arrested 37 Palestinians overnight in the West Bank.
"Thirty-seven Palestinians suspected of belonging to terrorist organisations were arrested...in a widespread operation by security forces in the West Bank," said an army spokesman.
Last Wednesday's double suicide bombing in Jerusalem's main outdoor market killed 15 people including the two attackers and prompted Israel to suspend peace talks with the Palestinians.
Hefetz said Israeli officials still had no lead in their investigation into the identity of the bombers.

A leaflet issued in the name of the Islamic militant Hamas group calimed responsibility for the bombings and gave an ultimatum to Israel to release all Palestinian prisoners by 9 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Sunday or face more attacks.
An Israeli official said Israel had doubts about the authenticity of the leaflet.
